newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale considers food security reserve.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale considers food security reserve.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Saturday he was ready to consider building a food security reserve to fight world hunger.

"We are prepared to engage in dialogue with our fellow exporters and with the world importers to try to find a way to build ourselves a cushion of world food supplies," Goodale told delegates at the annual Canadian Farm Writers' conference on global food security here.
The United Nation's Food and Agriculture Organization plans a conference on food security in Rome next month. The agency estimates 800 million people are malnurished.
The conferences come at a time when world wheat reserves are at a historic lows and grain prices at 20-year highs.

"Many say (a reserve) simply would not work. They say a buffer or a reserve would over hang the market and cause distortions and maybe they're right but when 800 million people go hungry in this world it at least behoves us all to try harder to come to grips with the issue," he said.
